Use the staged JSON and source registry as the current report authority.

Audience: a smart practice owner who wants to know exactly what each number means, where it came from, how it was calculated, why the inputs are logical, and what would change the conclusion. The document should be complete but readable, approximately 6 to 12 Letter pages when printed.

Required content:
- Cover with Vintage Optical, Morton, current date, Internal publish-candidate, Project Room review required, public-only, Confidence C, and no external actions.
- How to read this analysis: raw facts vs directional bands vs derived scores vs structural numbers. State that all displayed scores are higher = better.
- A Number map that lists every substantive page family: Client Opportunity 54/100; Market Demand-Supply 57/100; internal calculation input Competitive Pressure 57; Room to Win 43/100; Practice Competitiveness 58/100; Digital Presence 57/100; specialty scores 52/100, 52/100, 51/100; 2025 city estimate 17,565; historical 2024 estimate 17,557; 25.9%; 23.1%; 4.07 routed minutes; 20-minute primary and 30-minute extended method; exactly 3 Tier 1, 3 Tier 2, 3 Fix Cards, 3 specialty lanes, and a 30-day measurement window.
- Headline scores: show every canonical component, band, weight, contribution, full-precision total, rounding, result, source IDs, why each band was assigned, and what is unknown. State allowed bands exactly 20, 35, 50, 65, 80. Explain neutral unknown 50 as missing-evidence handling, not measured average performance. Include 100 - 57 = 43.
- Specialty opportunities: full component derivations for dry eye, myopia, and specialty contact lenses, with why each is RESEARCH NEXT rather than a forecast or white-space claim.
- Public facts and routes: explain 17,565 from S17 official 2025 PEP, 17,557 as the frozen 2024-vintage historical value, 25.9% and 23.1% from S14, and 4.07 minutes from R01 (244.3 seconds / 60 = 4.0717, rounded to 4.07). Clearly say city context is not a drive-time catchment and the bounded routes are not a complete supply census.
- Fix Card formulas: explain every displayed formula and each numerator/denominator. Define zero denominator handling as null / not calculable, never zero. State plug-in measurement, not a forecast. Explain the three-card, three-lane, one-table, and 30-day structural/plan counts.
- Structural numbers and identifiers: explain section 1/2/3, TIER 1/2, F-001/002/003, source IDs, the 100-point scale, 605 address, and 2026 copyright so the reader understands which numbers are not measurements.
- Logical consistency checks: reconcile why Market 57 can coexist with Room 43, Practice 58, Opportunity 54, and Digital 57; show that updating 17,557 to 17,565 changes no directional band or score; explain every shared or repeated score value; name disconfirmers and what new evidence could move each score.
- What we do not know: catchment population, complete supply, providers, VDU, peer-normalized reputation, live access, conversion, capacity, outcomes, referrals, economics, and execution capacity.
- Source dictionary: all 24 registered IDs with clickable public URLs, claim use, confidence, and limitation. Distinguish saved/frozen receipt paths from external links.

HTML requirements: self-contained print design except relative assets/mybcat-logo.png; @page size: Letter with print margins; page counter/footer; professional restrained MyBCAT visual system; readable tables with repeated headers; avoid clipped rows and awkward page breaks; at least 13 unique data-number-id attributes on substantive number sections; every source ID is a clickable link. Markdown and HTML must contain equivalent facts. Use standard hyphens, not em dashes. explainer_build_report.md must list inputs, number families covered, logical decisions, limitations, and external actions: none.
